36. Since 2017 I have met Gordon several times. All of these relate to instances when Gordon invited me to attend tender interviews with him, so I may assist with explaining the scope of work to be provided by China Status to his potential client.

37. My main contact at PC&E was Gordon. I knew him as a project manager of PC&E, and I have since learned from hearing materials that he was also a director of PC&E.

38. I also know another individual from PC&E, namely Mr Cheung, also known as “Ah Chung” (呀忠), who is a foreman of PC&E.

39. I had always understood and believed that PC&E was a RFSIC. Gordon had consistently told me that “Prestige”(“宏業”) was an RFSIC. I can recall that, during certain tender interviews which I attended with him, he always represented to others that “Prestige”(“宏業”) was a RFSIC. In the interviews, there was also a document introducing “Prestige”(“宏業”) which stated that it was a RFSIC. I had further checked the List of Registered Fire Service Installation Contractors (註冊消防裝置承辦商名單), and I recall seeing “Prestige”(“宏業”) on that list. Accordingly, I believed that PC&E was a RFSIC.

40. In the course of preparing this statement, I checked the List of Registered Fire Service Installation Contractors (註冊消防裝置承辦商名單)(at Annexure-1) and noted that:

(a) Prestige Constructions & Engineering Co. Limited (宏業建築工程有限公司) is not on the list; and  
(b) Prestige Construction & Fire Engineering Co. Limited (宏業建築及消防工程有限公司) is on the list.

41. China Status’s previous dealings with PC&E include:

(a) a project at Mayland Court in Causeway Bay;  
(b) a project at Chung Sing Building in Tai Kok Tsui; and
